overview: Tonga is an island country in the South Pacific and the only kingdom among the Pacific island nations. Its capital, Nuku'alofa, is on the main island of Tongatapu. Tonga was never colonised, although it was a British protected state until 1970. It has about 170 islands, fewer than 40 of which are lived on.

geography.text: Tonga's islands are a mix of low coral islands and higher volcanic ones. Underwater volcanoes are active nearby: in 2022 the eruption of Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai was one of the most powerful volcanic eruptions in recent history and sent a tsunami across the Pacific.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical, slightly cooler than other Pacific islands.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Humpback whales come to breed between July and October.

history.text: Tonga was settled about 3,000 years ago, and its Tu'i Tonga kings later ruled a sea-based empire across much of the South Pacific. King George Tupou I united Tonga and gave it a constitution in 1875. It became a British protected state in 1900 but was never colonised, and regained full independence in 1970.

events.title: The 'Friendly Islands'
events.text: James Cook visits and gives Tonga its English nickname.

events.title: Constitution
events.text: King George Tupou I gives Tonga a written constitution.

events.title: British protection
events.text: Tonga becomes a British protected state.

events.title: Full independence
events.text: Tonga regains full control of its affairs.

events.title: Volcanic eruption
events.text: A huge undersea eruption and tsunami hit Tonga.

government.text: Tonga is the only kingdom in the Pacific. The King is head of state and still holds significant power. Since reforms in 2010, most members of parliament are elected by the people, while some are chosen by the nobles, and parliament chooses the Prime Minister.

economy.text: Tonga's economy depends heavily on money from Tongans living abroad, mostly in New Zealand, Australia and the United States. Farming, fishing and tourism are also important. A volcanic eruption and tsunami in 2022 caused major damage.

culture.text: Tonga was never colonised, and its monarchy has deep roots. Tongans make tapa cloth from bark and wear ta'ovala, woven mats wrapped around the waist, on formal occasions. In 2022 the Hunga Tonga eruption was the biggest explosion in the atmosphere ever recorded by modern instruments.

items.title: Tapa cloth
items.text: Painted bark cloth used in ceremonies.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Lu pulu, corned beef with taro leaves and coconut cream.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Lakalaka, a sung dance listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On Sundays almost everything closes for church and family meals.

sport.text: Rugby union is the national sport. Pita Taufatofua became famous for carrying Tonga's flag shirtless and covered in oil at the 2016 Olympics. Many Tongans play rugby league and union around the world.

items.title: Pita Taufatofua
items.text: Competed in taekwondo, cross-country skiing and kayaking at the Olympics.
Tonga beat the USA and Samoa at the Rugby World Cup.

didYouKnow: Tonga is the only Pacific island kingdom.
Tonga was never colonised by a European power.

keyPeople.name: Queen Sālote Tupou III
keyPeople.text: Won hearts at Elizabeth II's coronation in 1953.

keyPeople.name: Pita Taufatofua
keyPeople.text: Competed in taekwondo, cross-country skiing and kayaking.
